title: QQQ ETF Pegs New High: Best Large-Cap Growth Fund Or Tech Sector Star?
summary: The PowerShares QQQ ETF has been the best-performing large-cap growth fund over the past 10 years, with an average annual gain of 12.8%. While it has strong performance, some experts view it more as a technology sector fund due to its heavy tech weighting (over 50%), suggesting it's better suited for a satellite role in a diversified portfolio rather than a core holding. The article also highlights QQQ's broader exposure to "tech innovators" that blur traditional sector lines and its potential benefits from cash repatriation under President Trump.

title: Microsoft, Toyota announce new licensing agreement for connected car IP
summary: Microsoft and Toyota have announced a new patent licensing agreement covering connected car technologies, building on their existing partnership. This agreement is part of Microsoft's broader initiative to encourage IP licensing for its connected car innovations, with a focus on cloud-based solutions and advanced in-car capabilities. The article also touches upon a legal issue concerning vehicle ownership and software modifications, as exemplified by Deere & Company.

title: Iron Mountain Secures Wind Power for Its Trio of Data Centers
summary: Iron Mountain has committed to powering its data centers entirely with renewable energy, signing a 15-year agreement for wind power in Pennsylvania. This move aligns the company with other mega-data center providers in prioritizing renewable sources, especially to serve major clients like Amazon and Microsoft, despite potential shifts in federal climate policy. The company projects that by 2018, solar and wind power will cover two-thirds of its North American electricity needs.

title: Here's What a $1,000 Investment in Amazon's 1997 Debut Is Worth Today
summary: This article examines the impressive growth of an early investment in Amazon.com Inc. since its 1997 IPO. It details how a $1,000 investment, despite early operating losses and multiple stock splits, would have grown to over half a million dollars by 2017 due to Amazon's aggressive expansion and market dominance. The piece highlights Amazon's journey from an online bookseller to a major e-commerce and tech giant, contrasting its performance with the broader retail sector.

title: DXC Technology Launches to Lead Digital Transformations, Helping Global Enterprises and Public Sector Clients to Thrive on Change
summary: DXC Technology officially launched as a leading independent IT services company, formed from the merger of CSC and HPE Enterprise Services. It aims to help global enterprises and public sector clients with digital transformations, offering extensive services, a large partner network, and a global footprint. The company debuted on the NYSE under the ticker symbol "DXC," with annual revenues of $25 billion and approximately 170,000 employees.

title: Amazon Alexa has become one of my BFFs, says Omnicom Media chief
summary: Omnicom Media Group's Philippa Brown highlights how Amazon's Alexa has transformed her work by enabling multitasking and streamlining daily tasks. She notes Alexa's continuous learning and expanding functionalities, impacting sectors like automotive, energy, and travel. Brown emphasizes the growing importance of voice-activated search for brands and anticipates significant developments, particularly in the automotive industry.

title: The five-minute CIO: Dharmesh Shah, CTO, HubSpot
summary: Dharmesh Shah, co-founder and CTO of HubSpot, discusses the company's origins, its product development ethos, and the expansion of its European headquarters in Dublin. He highlights HubSpot's focus on creating intuitive software and its optimistic view on the future of AI and conversational user interfaces, particularly with the GrowthBot product. Shah also touches upon the challenges and successes of building a strong employer brand in Dublin and the technical hurdles of scaling their platform.

title: Google Espresso to boost delivery of cloud-based application services
summary: Google has introduced Espresso, a new peering architecture unveiled at the Open Networking Summit, designed to enhance the delivery of cloud-based application services from Google Cloud. Espresso improves application performance by expanding Google's software-defined networking infrastructure to the network edge and prioritizing traffic based on latency requirements. This system routes 20% of Google's immense internet traffic and replaces traditional routers with software-controlled switches for greater efficiency and reliability.

title: Fortinet upgrades for better cloud, SD-WAN protection
summary: Fortinet has released FortiOS 5.6, an upgraded operating system enabling unified security management across cloud assets and SD-WAN environments, including AWS and Azure. The company also announced FortiCASB, a platform for securing SaaS applications, which integrates with the Fortinet Security Fabric for consistent policy enforcement. These enhancements aim to provide comprehensive protection and simplified management for complex network infrastructures.

title: Riverbed enables WNS to up application speed 3X, better staff productivity & customer liking
summary: WNS (Holdings) Limited has significantly improved application speed by 3x and email/file downloads by 10x using Riverbed SteelHead solution, leading to enhanced staff productivity and customer satisfaction. The deployment eliminated the need for expensive bandwidth upgrades, offering substantial cost savings and drastically reducing IT help tickets related to slow performance. WNS plans to leverage this foundation for future IT innovations, including a migration to Office 365, confident in SteelHead's ability to maintain performance.

title: Pegasystems Introduces Pega Intelligent Virtual Assistant
summary: Pegasystems Inc. launched Pega Intelligent Virtual Assistant, an AI-powered bot designed to transform applications into smart assistants across various channels like SMS, email, Facebook, and Alexa. This new solution aims to overcome the limitations of current chatbots by providing sophisticated, human-like interactions for personalized customer service and task completion. The Pega Intelligent Virtual Assistant is built into the Pega Platform, leveraging AI, natural language processing, and a unified architecture to offer a comprehensive bot solution for enterprises.

title: Microsoft announces artificial intelligence-based products and services
summary: Microsoft announced several new AI-based products and services, including SQL Server 2017 with built-in AI, Microsoft R Server 9.1, Azure cognitive services, and Cortana intelligence solution templates. These offerings aim to help organizations leverage data-driven intelligence for digital transformation and enable developers to create next-generation enterprise-grade AI applications. The new SQL Server will be compatible with Windows, Linux, and Docker containers, broadening its applicability.

title: Amazon blazes a trail to the next frontier in AI: the cloud
summary: Amazon is making a significant push into artificial intelligence, particularly by leveraging its AWS cloud to democratize machine learning for developers. CEO Jeff Bezos views machine learning as crucial for the company's future, powering internal operations and customer-facing services like Alexa and Amazon Go, and setting Amazon up as a platform company in AI. The company is focusing on making deep learning accessible, supporting various frameworks, and addressing scalability challenges for petabytes of data.

title: Feature: Local business consultant licensed to operate Franklin Covey-Guyana
summary: Dr. Rosh Khan, an internationally certified business consultant, has acquired the license to operate Franklin Covey in Guyana. This global leader in management and organizational behavior aims to revolutionize how companies operate by focusing on lasting changes in human behavior. Khan believes Franklin Covey's result-based approach, focusing on organizational behavior change and capacity building, is crucial for Guyana's development.

title: Nokia, Onetime Cell-Phone Champ, Turns to Bathroom Scales
summary: Nokia, once a dominant force in cellphones, is attempting a consumer-electronics comeback by selling products like $100 bathroom scales. This strategy leverages brand recognition from Withings, a digital-health-device company it acquired. Nokia previously exited the personal device market in 2014, shifting its focus to cellular tower equipment.

title: Microsoft appoints globally respected regulator to privacy leadership role
summary: Microsoft has appointed Julie Brill, former Commissioner of the U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC), to lead its Privacy and Regulatory Affairs Group as corporate vice president and deputy general counsel. Brill, recognized for her expertise in privacy and data protection, will be responsible for shaping the company’s global legal, regulatory, and public policy response on critical issues facing the technology sector. Her role will also involve working with external stakeholders and Microsoft's engineering groups to build strong privacy protection into products and services, particularly in light of new standards like the European Union General Data Protection Regulation.

title: These Are The Best-Paying Internships In America
summary: A new survey by Glassdoor reveals that tech companies, particularly Facebook Inc., offer the highest-paying internships in America, with some interns earning $8,000 a month. While tech firms dominate the top spots, Exxon Mobil Corp. is noted as the highest-paying non-tech company. Beyond generous salaries, many of these internships also cover lodging, meals, and transportation, especially in high-cost areas like San Francisco.

title: Microsoft unveils new effort to teach kids to code through Minecraft
summary: Microsoft is launching a new initiative to teach children how to code through its popular game, Minecraft Education Edition. This will be achieved via a "Codebuilder" add-on that allows students to program within the game using tools like the Tynker plugin and visualize code execution with the "Agent." Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella emphasized the company's commitment to fostering creativity and empowering users through technology.

title: Adobe bets big on cloud computing for marketing, creative professionals
summary: Adobe Systems is significantly focusing on its cloud computing offerings, namely Experience Cloud and Creative Cloud, for marketing and creative professionals, with a strong emphasis on its partnership with Microsoft Azure. The company sees immense growth potential, particularly in India, driven by the increasing demand for digital transformation and customer experience solutions. Despite market challenges such as integration issues and high costs, Adobe, alongside Salesforce.com and Oracle, dominates the digital marketing hub market.

title: Apple becomes first $800 billion company with stock price increase
summary: Apple Inc. briefly surpassed an $800 billion market capitalization, becoming the first company to do so, following a stock price increase to $153.70 per share on Monday. The surge was attributed to a positive research note from Drexel Hamilton's Brian White, who set an ambitious price target of $185 to $202 per share, suggesting Apple could reach a trillion-dollar valuation. Despite concerns about the consumer electronics sector, Apple's ability to seamlessly integrate hardware, software, and services has demonstrated its market resilience.

title: FedEx hit as NSA-linked ransomware spreads around the world
summary: FedEx announced it was a victim of the "WannaCry" ransomware attack, which is rapidly spreading globally and is linked to leaked NSA data. The malware, exploiting an NSA exploit called 'EternalBlue,' targets Microsoft Windows systems, encrypting files and demanding a $300 Bitcoin ransom. The attack has affected organizations in at least 70 countries, including the U.K.'s National Health Service, and highlights the urgent need for robust cybersecurity measures and skilled professionals.

title: If You Invested in Amazon at Its IPO, You Would Be a Millionaire Today
summary: This article highlights the hypothetical massive returns an early investment in Amazon's IPO would have yielded, illustrating that a $5,000 investment 20 years ago would now be worth $2.4 million. It explores how this reflects on investors like Warren Buffett, who regretted not buying Amazon early, and details the company's tumultuous stock performance, including its dot-com bubble rise and subsequent dip, before its massive growth to a $457.9 billion market cap.

title: 'WannaCry' attack sends cybersecurity stocks higher
summary: The widespread 'WannaCry' ransomware attack led to a significant surge in cybersecurity stock prices on Monday as investors sought safety in the sector. Despite the attack slowing, major companies like Hitachi reported related computer problems, prompting investors to boost shares of cybersecurity firms such as PureFunds ISE Cyber Security, Palo Alto Networks, Symantec, Cisco Systems, Fortinet, and Proofpoint, all closing notably higher. Microsoft also saw a fractional increase in its shares as it worked to contain the attack.

title: Threat Brief: WanaCrypt0r– What We Know
summary: This Unit 42 threat brief details the WanaCrypt0r ransomware attack, which emerged on May 12, 2017, and spread through the exploitation of the ETERNALBLUE vulnerability (CVE-2017-0144) in Microsoft Windows. The article clarifies propagation methods, provides Palo Alto Networks' protection recommendations, and analyzes the financial impact and "killswitch" mechanism of the malware. It also discusses various theories for initial delivery and lateral movement, emphasizing the importance of applying the Microsoft patch MS17-010.

title: Top 20 companies in Houston for job-seeking graduates
summary: This article lists top companies in Houston for recent graduates looking for jobs, highlighting the city's strong economy in oil/energy, healthcare, and IT. It names companies identified by LinkedIn and Glassdoor as top hirers of new graduates and best places to work. The article also mentions the Memorial Hermann Hospital System as the area's largest employer.

title: Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff says his company is 'crushing Oracle'
summary: Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff stated that his company is "crushing Oracle" and other competitors like SAP and Microsoft, following a strong first-quarter earnings beat and raised guidance for fiscal year 2018. Benioff attributed Salesforce's growth to its recent strategic acquisitions and expanded partnerships, highlighting significant customer wins and market share gains. The company's stock saw a 3 percent rise in after-hours trading due to the positive earnings report.

title: HP reveals new Windows 10 devices built for creativity at Cannes Film Festival
summary: HP Inc. announced a new premium portfolio of Windows 10 devices—the Spectre x2, ENVY x360, and ENVY laptops—at the Cannes Film Festival, targeting digital creators. These devices ship with the Windows 10 Creators Update and offer features like Windows Hello, Microsoft Edge, and Cortana. The announcement details specifications and pricing for each model, emphasizing performance, design, and creative functionality.

(BMRA), including real-time stock price, historical performance, key statistics, company overview, recent news, and earnings trends. summary: This article examines the paradox created by OFCCP's diversity hiring enforcement, particularly focusing on the Palantir settlement and Oracle lawsuit. The author suggests methods for companies to better comply with OFCCP regulations while navigating these challenges.

title: Speeds of storage networking technologies rise as flash use spikes
summary: This article traces the evolution of Ethernet speeds, starting from 10 Mbps in the 1980s to the development of 400 Gbps standards. It highlights the role of hyperscale data centers in driving demand for higher-speed, more cost-effective networking and the efforts by consortiums and IEEE to develop new Ethernet standards like 25 Gbps, 50 Gbps, 100 Gbps, 200 Gbps, and 400 Gbps. The article also touches upon the development of 2.5 Gbps and 5 Gbps Ethernet for LANs to support faster Wi-Fi without requiring extensive cabling upgrades.

title: Mary Barra shapes a new GM: Fast, focused and decisive
summary: Mary Barra has transformed General Motors in 3½ years into a more decisive, focused, and profit-driven company. Under her leadership, GM has prioritized customer satisfaction and profitability over sales volume, leading to divestments from unprofitable markets and aggressive investments in new technologies like autonomous and electric vehicles. This shift aims to make GM the "most valued automotive company" by all stakeholders.

title: How former Apple CEO Sculley helped usher in the personal computing era
summary: Former Apple CEO John Sculley discusses his tenure at Apple, highlighting how he and Steve Jobs focused on making computers personal and accessible to non-technical users. He also reflects on Apple's challenges against industry standards and shares his current work in fintech and healthcare, applying technology to disrupt traditional industries.

title: HPE Looks Ahead To Composable Infrastructure, Persistent Memory
summary: Facing challenges in the server market, Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) is focusing on composable infrastructure, next-generation ProLiant servers, and persistent memory. Among new offerings, HPE will be rolling out Intel Skylake Xeon-powered servers, OneView 3.1 for resource pooling, and Scalable Persistent Memory leveraging NVDIMM technology. The company is also emphasizing silicon-level security and expanding its flash storage portfolio.

title: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE), an eight step quick history
summary: This article provides an eight-step history of Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) since its split in November 2015, detailing its strategic divestitures and acquisitions. It highlights how HPE refocused on core corporate and enterprise clientele, strengthening its server, storage, and networking offerings through key moves in high-performance computing, cloud analytics, security, hyper-converged infrastructure, and flash storage. The strategic changes aimed to make HPE a more "laser focused" organization to meet enterprise IT demands.

title: Quadrant Homes Launches New Standard Home Automation Package
summary: Quadrant Homes is introducing a new standard Home Technology Package in all its new residences, including smart lighting, virtual assistant connectors, and built-in access points. This decision is driven by increasing consumer demand for connected homes, particularly in the tech-savvy Seattle area. The package integrates products from multiple companies like Ring, Schlage, Liftmaster, and Nest to offer comprehensive security, comfort, and connectivity features.

title: Plantronics and Dolby Team Up to Usher in a New Dimension of Sound
summary: Plantronics and Dolby Laboratories Inc. have partnered to release a new line of high-end RIG headsets for Xbox One, Project Scorpio, and Windows 10 platforms. These headsets will feature Dolby Atmos® audio technology, providing spatial audio for a more immersive gaming experience. The new models, including the RIG 400LX, RIG 600LX, and RIG 800LX, will be available in fall 2017 with prices ranging from $99.99 to $149.99.

title: DuPont Fabros Deal Gives Digital Realty More Firepower in the War for Cloud Deals
summary: Digital Realty Trust's acquisition of DuPont Fabros Technology for $7.6 billion significantly expands its footprint in key North American data center markets, strengthening its ability to secure large deals with hyper-scale cloud platforms like Microsoft, Apple, and Salesforce. This merger also preempts competitors and makes Digital Realty the largest multi-tenant data center provider in North America. Despite this consolidation, intense competition within the hyper-scale data center market is expected to continue.

title: The Gartner It Security Approach For The Digital Age
summary: Gartner advocates for a continuous adaptive risk and trust assessment (CARTA) approach to IT security in the digital age, moving beyond traditional binary security models. This approach emphasizes adaptive security across "Run," "Build," and "Plan" phases, integrating analytics and automation to manage risks associated with digital business opportunities like cloud services, big data, mobile, and DevOps. The CARTA mindset aims to enable organizations to embrace new opportunities more readily by continuously monitoring and assessing risks.

title: SCOTUS Delivers Win for Microsoft Defendants
summary: The Supreme Court ruled that class action plaintiffs cannot immediately appeal the denial of class certification by voluntarily dismissing their individual claims, thereby upholding the final-judgment rule and the discretionary appellate review process under Rule 23(f). This decision is seen as a victory for class action defendants, reaffirming that class certification decisions are interlocutory and emphasizing the need for evenhanded treatment of all parties in such cases. The Court recognized the "reverse death knell" effect, where class certification can pressure defendants into settling, providing them with a stronger basis for seeking interlocutory appeal.

title: Accelerating Security Innovation: Introducing the Palo Alto Networks Application Framework
summary: Palo Alto Networks has introduced its new Application Framework, designed to accelerate security innovation by allowing customers to rapidly adopt new security technologies delivered as cloud-based apps. This framework, built on their Next-Generation Security Platform, enables any provider, partner, MSSP, or customer to build apps. To support this initiative, Palo Alto Networks also announced a $20 million security venture fund to fuel the development of innovative security applications.

title: How Salesforce Gained Its Moat
summary: Salesforce.com has established a "wide moat" in the customer relationship management (CRM) industry through its strong network effect, brand, and high customer switching costs. Despite increasing competition from companies like Microsoft, Salesforce maintains its leadership position with a significant market share. The company's exponential revenue growth and long-term contracts suggest continued strength, although the competitive nature of the CRM market poses an ongoing threat.

title: How to Short Technology Stocks with ETFs
summary: The technology sector has shown signs of losing steam due to overvaluation concerns and profit-taking, leading investors to consider short positions. This article explores several ETFs that offer inverse exposure to the tech sector for investors looking to capitalize on a bearish outlook. It highlights ETFs with varying inverse exposures, including those focusing on the broader tech sector and the semiconductor industry, noting their suitability for short-term traders.

title: |How Insurance Giant Allstate Is Using Cloud Tech to Build New Businesses
summary: |Allstate, an 86-year-old insurance giant, is leveraging cloud technology to innovate and compete with startups. Through its CompoZed Labs unit, Allstate has dramatically sped up software development, allowing for quick testing and deployment of new services like an improved roadside assistance app. This strategic use of cloud-agnostic tools enables flexibility and fosters creativity within the company.

title: Invesco NASDAQ Internet ETF (PNQI) Holdings
summary: This article provides detailed holdings and performance data for the Invesco NASDAQ Internet ETF (PNQI). It lists the top 10 holdings, sector weightings, and overall portfolio composition, showing a strong focus on technology and consumer cyclical companies. The ETF aims to track internet-related businesses listed on major U.S. exchanges.

title: Booking.com Is Expanding Beyond Hotels and Into Flights, Cars and Restaurants
summary: Booking.com is expanding its offerings beyond hotels to include flights, car rentals, and restaurant reservations, integrating services from sister companies within the Priceline Group. This move signifies a strategic shift for Booking.com to become a more comprehensive online travel agency, aiming to capture a larger share of the traveler journey amidst competition from full-service rivals like Expedia and Ctrip. The new tabs are currently part of a test to gauge their performance and user adoption.

title: Box and Microsoft partner for cloud content management with Azure
summary: Box and Microsoft have announced an expanded partnership to offer Box cloud content management with Azure to enterprise customers. Box will leverage Azure as a strategic public cloud platform, with shared go-to-market investments and future integration of Azure's AI and machine learning capabilities with Box's platform. This collaboration aims to provide businesses with enhanced cloud content management, advanced machine learning features, and expanded global data storage options through Box Zones.

title: The 50 Smartest Companies in 2017, According to MIT Experts
summary: MIT Technology Review released its annual list of the world's 50 smartest companies for 2017, based on business savvy and creative use of emerging technology. Nvidia topped the list for its AI software and growing AI businesses, with a valuation of $90.9 billion. The list also includes major companies like Apple and Facebook, alongside newcomers such as Face++, Carbon, and Desktop Metal.

title: Evidence, Inc.
summary: TASER International rebranded as Axon Enterprise Inc. to emphasize its growing body camera business and launched an initiative offering free body cameras and cloud storage to U.S. police departments for a year. This move has sparked controversy regarding competitive practices and concerns about a single corporation controlling sensitive police evidence. The article also touches on Axon's future plans for AI integration and the debate around body camera transparency and usage, noting that Tasers still generate the majority of Axon's revenue despite the push for body cameras.

title: SAS ranked a Leader in real-time interaction management by independent research firm
summary: SAS has been recognized as a Leader in The Forrester Wave™: Real-Time Interaction Management, Q1 2024, highlighting its use of responsible AI in enterprise RTIM decisioning. The report notes SAS's roadmap to make predictive and generative AI more accessible to knowledge workers. SAS leverages its advanced analytics to enhance RTIM use cases with real-time alerts and decisions across areas like credit, fraud, and risk.

title: Five9 Takes on the World
summary: Five9 announced significant architectural changes to its Virtual Contact Center (VCC) application as part of its Summer Release 2017. These changes aim to enhance the platform for enterprise and global scalability, moving towards a microservices-based architecture and introducing new voice points of presence. The update also includes tighter integrations with WFO solutions from partners and with Salesforce and Microsoft Skype for Business, signaling Five9's intent to target the large enterprise contact center market.

title: Intel rolls out new chips in battle for data center business
summary: Intel Corp. announced a new line of Xeon Scalable Processor chips designed for data centers, aiming to compete with Advanced Micro Devices and other chip providers in the lucrative cloud computing market. These new chips offer enhanced support for next-generation computing applications like artificial intelligence and driverless cars, with Google Cloud Platform being the first data center to adopt them. The article highlights the competitive landscape, noting AMD's new data center processor and the growing trend of large internet companies designing their own hardware to push Intel on pricing.

title: Microsoft’s board adopts board tenure policy
summary: Microsoft's Board of Directors has adopted a new board tenure policy, targeting an average tenure of 10 years or less for independent directors. This formalizes an existing practice and aims to balance the need for experienced directors with a desire for fresh perspectives and board refreshment. The decision was influenced by investor feedback and emphasizes the importance of diversity on the board.

title: Tech Moves: Microsoft bringing in GE tech executive to be corporate VP of U.S. division
summary: Microsoft announced that Kate Johnson, a current executive with GE Digital, will join the company as president and corporate vice president of its U.S. division, starting September 8th. Johnson brings over 20 years of business and technology experience, having previously held senior vice president roles at Oracle and executive positions at GE, where she also championed diversity initiatives. Her new responsibilities at Microsoft were not immediately detailed.

title: Baidu and Microsoft join forces in the intelligent cloud to advance autonomous driving
summary: Baidu and Microsoft have announced a partnership to advance autonomous driving globally. Microsoft will provide its Azure cloud platform to support Baidu's Apollo open platform outside of China, offering a secure and trustworthy public cloud for Apollo partners. This collaboration aims to leverage Microsoft's AI, machine learning, and deep neural network capabilities to accelerate the development of safer autonomous vehicles.

title: New App Helps Blind People Know the World Around Them
summary: Microsoft has released a new, free app called "Seeing AI" for Apple's iPhone and iPad, designed to assist blind and visually impaired individuals. The app utilizes a camera and artificial intelligence to identify objects, people, documents, and even emotions, announcing them aloud to the user. Seeing AI also features capabilities like reading product bar codes, menu items, and soon, banknote values, significantly enhancing independence for its users.

title: Amazon acquires Santa Barbara start-up Graphiq to try to bolster Alexa
summary: Amazon acquired Santa Barbara start-up Graphiq in May 2017 for an estimated $50 million to enhance its Alexa virtual assistant and other services. Graphiq, founded as FindTheBest, specialized in organizing and connecting data to simplify online research, having previously developed tools for news publishers and an Alexa app. The acquisition brings Graphiq's data analysis technology and its employees into Amazon, strengthening Amazon's competitive position against other major tech companies in delivering quick answers to consumer queries.

title: Microsoft and AIS engage in Thailand’s first partnership to provide Thai customers with world-class reliability and security on the Microsoft Cloud
summary: Microsoft and AIS have formed a partnership in Thailand to provide secure and reliable access to Microsoft cloud services for Thai customers. This collaboration will enhance cloud-based productivity for both consumers and businesses by integrating the AIS network with Microsoft's cloud platform, offering improved performance, cost reduction, and robust security. The agreement positions AIS as Thailand's first Microsoft cloud service partner with optimized integration for Microsoft's cloud facilities in Singapore and Hong Kong.

title: Smart Vacuum Cleaners Making Map Of Your Home — And Wants to Sell It
summary: iRobot, the company behind the Roomba vacuum cleaner, is reportedly planning to sell the home mapping data collected by its devices to third-party companies like Apple, Amazon, Microsoft, and Google. While this raises significant privacy concerns, proponents suggest the data could enhance the functionality of other smart home devices. iRobot CEO Colin Angle states that this would only happen with users' consent and could lead to a more integrated smart home ecosystem.

title: Amazon’s Jeff Bezos is now the world’s richest man
summary: Jeff Bezos, founder of Amazon.com Inc., surpassed Bill Gates to become the world's richest person due to a surge in Amazon's share price ahead of its earnings report. His net worth reached $90.9 billion, primarily driven by Amazon's 40% stock increase this year and the success of its Prime service and cloud-computing division, Amazon Web Services. This marks a significant shift in global wealth rankings, with Bezos leapfrogging Gates who had held the top spot since May 2013.

title: Microsoft OneDrive recognized as a Leader in Gartner Magic Quadrant for Content Collaboration Platforms
summary: Microsoft OneDrive has been recognized as a Leader in Gartner's 2017 Magic Quadrant Report for Content Collaboration Platforms, placing highest for Ability to Execute. This recognition highlights OneDrive's commitment to providing robust file sharing and collaboration capabilities, integrating seamlessly with Office 365 and supporting a wide range of file types, while offering strong security and deployment flexibility. The article emphasizes OneDrive's cloud leadership, compliance, and significant adoption among Fortune 500 companies.

title: Amazon’s Jeff Bezos becomes world’s richest, unseating Bill Gates
summary: Jeff Bezos, CEO of Amazon, has surpassed Bill Gates to become the world's richest person, with an estimated fortune of $90.6 billion. This rise is attributed to Amazon's significant stock jump and its aggressive expansion into various new markets beyond e-commerce. Meanwhile, Bill Gates, a prolific philanthropist, holds a net worth of $90.1 billion, having donated $31.1 billion to charity through 2016.

title: Jeff Bezos overtakes Bill Gates as world’s richest person
summary: Jeff Bezos, founder of Amazon.com Inc., surpassed Bill Gates as the world's richest person on July 27, 2017, due to a surge in Amazon's stock ahead of its earnings report. Bezos's net worth reached $90.9 billion, slightly above Gates's $90.7 billion. Investors were scrutinizing Amazon Prime subscriptions and the performance of its cloud-computing division, Amazon Web Services.

title: World's Richest Person? Not Bill Gates, But Jeff Bezos
summary: Jeff Bezos, the founder and CEO of Amazon.com, has surpassed Bill Gates of Microsoft to become the world's richest person. His net worth reached over $90.5 billion due to Amazon's stock prices, making him the first multi-billionaire to overtake Gates in seven years. Bezos owns about 17 percent of Amazon and also has holdings in The Washington Post and Blue Origin.

title: Microsoft’s new corporate vision: artificial intelligence is in and mobile is out
summary: Microsoft's annual report reveals a significant shift in its corporate vision, highlighting artificial intelligence as a core focus while diminishing the emphasis on "mobile-first." This change aligns with the company's recent investments in AI, including a 5,000-person engineering team and AI-focused product announcements, and its retreat from the smartphone market. The new vision emphasizes an "intelligent cloud and an intelligent edge" where AI drives insights and user experiences span across devices.

title: Carnival Corporation

title: How to Think About the Problem of Corporate Offshore Cash: Lessons from Microsoft
summary: This article examines Microsoft's offshore cash holdings, highlighting its claim that virtually all earnings are foreign despite its American roots. It reveals Microsoft has $142 billion in "permanently reinvested" foreign earnings, avoiding $45 billion in U.S. taxes, and questions the legitimacy of these offshore profits. The piece argues that a significant portion of these funds are likely U.S.-sourced profits shifted offshore to evade taxes, making a strong case against tax holidays for repatriation.

title: AI Superstar Andrew Ng Is Democratizing Deep Learning With A New Online Course
summary: Andrew Ng, a co-founder of Google Brain and former head of AI at Baidu, is launching a new set of five interconnected online courses called "Deep Learning Specialization" through Coursera. Ng aims to train a massive new workforce in AI, believing it will transform the economy as electricity did a century ago. His new company, deeplearning.ai, seeks to make AI-powered solutions widely accessible, focusing on applications in healthcare, education, and transportation.

title: What’s Changed: 2017 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Data Integration Tools
summary: Gartner has released its 2017 Magic Quadrant for Data Integration Tools, evaluating 15 providers based on their ability to execute and completeness of vision. The report highlights Informatica and IBM as top leaders, with SAP, Talend, Oracle, and SAS also in the leaders bracket. Microsoft leads challengers, while Denodo shows strong momentum among visionaries, and Pentaho makes a return to the niche players quadrant.

title: RETO: ReTo Eco-Solutions Inc Latest Stock Price, Analysis, News and Trading Ideas
summary: This page provides the latest stock price, fundamental analysis, news, and trading ideas for ReTo Eco-Solutions Inc (RETO). As of the update, RETO's stock was trading at $1.14, down 5.00% overnight, with a market cap of $88.09M. The article also highlights recent company news, including a share combination, an acquisition, and equipment showcases.

title: Electronic Arts Inc. - NBA LIVE 18 Launches Groundbreaking Free Demo, Starting August 11
summary: Electronic Arts Inc. announced that a free demo for NBA LIVE 18 will launch on August 11th for Xbox One and PlayStation 4, allowing players to carry over their progress to the full game. Players who pre-order NBA LIVE 18 will receive a 33% discount. Houston Rockets star James Harden is featured as the cover athlete for NBA LIVE 18, which is set to launch on September 15th.

title: Two years in, Sundar Pichai facing his toughest moment as CEO
summary: Sundar Pichai, two years into his tenure as Google CEO, has overseen significant growth in AI and hardware, including the Pixel smartphone launch, and rapid Android expansion. Despite these successes, he is currently navigating significant internal controversies surrounding a sexism debate and a record fine from the European Commission. The article explores his achievements and challenges, particularly the recent internal cultural issues.

title: Introduction of Xbox One X & PS4 Pro Enables Lower Pricing of Base XO and PS4, Turtle Beach Believes
summary: Headset manufacturer Turtle Beach believes that the introduction of the Xbox One X and PS4 Pro will allow Microsoft and Sony to lower the prices of their standard Xbox One and PS4 models. This strategy is expected to make console gaming more accessible and boost headset sales for companies like Turtle Beach. The company sees a strong holiday season for their headset business due to these hardware refreshments and good sales of marquee game titles.

title: Microsoft CFO named to 3M's board
summary: Amy Hood, the chief financial officer at Microsoft Corp., has been elected to 3M Co.'s board of directors. This appointment brings a prominent tech executive to the board of the manufacturing conglomerate. The article includes related stories about other executives joining various company boards.

title: NetApp CEO on Amazon, Donald Trump, and Silicon Valley Hubris
summary: NetApp CEO George Kurian discusses the company's transformation from a hardware-focused business to one centered on software subscriptions, adapting to the rise of cloud computing led by Amazon. He also shares his views on President Trump's immigration policies, the misconceptions about Indian workers, and the culture of hubris in Silicon Valley. Kurian emphasizes the importance of data management as a strategic asset for businesses utilizing multiple cloud providers.

title: Microsoft CFO named to 3M's board
summary: 3M Co. has elected Amy E. Hood, the chief financial officer at Microsoft Corp., to its board of directors. Hood will serve on the 3M board’s finance committee, with her tenure effective immediately. She is recognized for her skills in strategic business development, finance, and digitization.

title: Equinix Invests $32 Million to Expand Footprint in Hong Kong with New Data Center Opening
summary: Equinix is investing $32 million to open its fifth International Business Exchange™ (IBX®) data center, HK5, in Hong Kong by Q4 2017. This new facility is designed to meet the high demand for interconnection, especially from financial services firms. HK5 will provide scalability, reliability, and access to diverse digital ecosystems, while also featuring green energy-efficient technologies.

title: Key Takeaways from Gartner’s New 2017 Access Management Magic Quadrant
summary: Gartner has released its first-ever Access Management (AM) Magic Quadrant (MQ), replacing the Identity and Access Management as a Service (IDaaS) MQ. The report evaluates 15 vendors based on their ability to execute and completeness of vision, with Microsoft, Oracle, IBM, CA Technologies, Okta, and Ping Identity leading the pack. The article highlights contextual access controls as a key differentiator and a future trend in AM.

title: Future Trends In The Gartner Hype Cycle For Emerging Technologies, 2017
summary: The 2017 Gartner Hype Cycle for Emerging Technologies highlights three megatrends: AI everywhere, transparently immersive experiences, and digital platforms, which are crucial for competitive advantage in the next 5-10 years. While artificial general intelligence (AGI) is still nascent, technologies like machine learning, blockchain, and augmented reality are progressing significantly. The article discusses the potential disruptive impact of these technologies across various industries and advises enterprises to strategically explore their applications and develop relevant strategies.

title: Lifted by its Mass. labs, chip maker AMD rebounds
summary: Chipmaker Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD) is experiencing a significant rebound, driven largely by innovation from its Boxborough, Massachusetts labs. After years of struggling against Intel and seeing its market share decline, AMD has launched powerful new CPU and GPU chips that are competitive with industry leaders and have led to increased revenue and a tenfold increase in market valuation. The Boxborough facility, which has grown to 400 employees, is credited with developing key technologies like the Zen and Vega processors, as well as custom chips for gaming consoles and servers.

title: SAP Leases Space at New Atlanta Office Building
summary: SAP has signed a 10-year lease for 43,800 square feet at 800 Avalon, a new mixed-use building in Alpharetta, Ga., marking its second location in metro Atlanta. This move will consolidate employees from two other offices and brings 800 Avalon's occupancy to 93 percent, joining other notable tenants like Microsoft and Spaces. The $73 million project, developed by Hines and Cousins Property, was completed in June 2017.

title: Adobe Systems CEO Touts 'Textbook Transition' To Cloud
summary: Adobe Systems CEO Shantanu Narayen discusses the company's successful transition to a cloud computing business model, emphasizing its role in digital transformation for companies. He highlights Adobe's focus on data, the integration of TubeMogul for video monetization, and the importance of R&D and corporate competitiveness for the tech industry.

title: 7 things to know about the Apple data center in Waukee
summary: Apple Inc. unveiled plans for a $1.375 billion data center in Waukee, Iowa, with CEO Tim Cook attending the announcement. The facility, slated to open in 2020, will be built on a 2,000-acre site, create 50 permanent jobs, and be powered by 100 percent renewable energy. Apple will receive over $213 million in state and local incentives, including tax credits and property tax abatements similar to those offered to other tech giants like Google, Microsoft, and Facebook for their Iowa data centers.

title: ProShares Ultra QQQ 2x Shares (QLD) Stock Price, Holdings, Dividend Yield
summary: This article provides a detailed profile of ProShares Ultra QQQ 2x Shares (QLD), including its current stock price, key statistics, dividend yield, and top holdings as of November 2025. It highlights the ETF's performance, fundamental data, and lists its major equity positions, such as NVIDIA, Apple, and Microsoft. The report also offers insight into the ETF's portfolio value, turnover rate, and historical data like PE and PB ratios.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Content Marketing: Should you Fight or Embrace it?, Part I
summary: This article explores the growing influence of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in content marketing, examining whether humans should resist or embrace it. It details how AI is being used for content generation, personalized news feeds, machine learning algorithms like Google's RankBrain, and smart advertising, while also addressing concerns about AI replacing human marketers. The author concludes that AI will likely assist human marketers by automating tasks rather than fully replacing them.

title: GE shifts strategy, financial targets for digital business after missteps
summary: General Electric Co is overhauling its digital business strategy, aiming to cut costs and boost profits under new CEO John Flannery, after its Predix software platform faced technical issues and slow revenue growth. The company is redefining digital revenue, focusing sales on existing customers, and considering partnerships or equity sales for the unit to improve financial performance and investor confidence. This strategic shift follows a 25 percent decline in GE's share price and represents a course correction for its ambitious digital industrial transformation.

title: State of Global Content Marketing: Highlights from Our Report
summary: This report highlights key content marketing trends from 2016, emphasizing the global dominance of mobile content consumption and the significant growth in video viewing across various regions. It also discusses the increasing importance of content marketing, the impact of ad blockers, and the most-read news stories which often revolved around tragedies and major political events.

title: Veeva: The Biggest Vertical SaaS Success Story of All Time So Far (Video + Pod)
summary: This article features a discussion with Peter Gassner, CEO and co-founder of Veeva, about the company's journey from a startup to a $35 billion cloud juggernaut specializing in pharma and life science applications. Gassner shares insights on Veeva's growth, its multi-product strategy, capital efficiency, and his philosophy on execution and pricing. He emphasizes the importance of not following the herd, working with engaged teams, and continuous learning through exploring "adjacent possible" ideas.

title: First Quantum Annealing Computer in the U.S. to have more than 2000 qubits installed and operational
summary: The Universities Space Research Association (USRA), in collaboration with NASA and Google Inc., has upgraded its quantum annealing computer to a D-Wave 2000Q system, now featuring over 2000 qubits. Located at NASA's Ames Research Center, this makes it the first such installation in the United States, promising to solve more complex optimization problems in various applications like machine learning and diagnostics. USRA is also offering 20% of computing time free of cost to university and industrial research organizations through a new Request for Proposals.

title: The curious case of HP, Autonomy and the scandal that won’t quit
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) has finally shed the legacy of its disastrous Autonomy acquisition with the spin-off of its software business, narrowing its focus to data center software and hardware. The article details the six-year scandal following HP's 2011 acquisition of Autonomy for $10.3 billion, which led to an $8.8 billion write-down, legal battles, and a PR war between HP and former Autonomy CEO Mike Lynch. While HPE has closed the book on its involvement with Autonomy, the legal case between HPE and Lynch over a $5.1 billion battle is set to continue.

title: HP Enterprise Acquires Cloud Technology Partners (CTP); Beware Channel Conflict -
summary: HP Enterprise (HPE) is acquiring Cloud Technology Partners (CTP), a consulting firm specializing in helping Fortune 500 companies migrate workloads to major cloud platforms like AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud. While CTP's CEO described the acquisition as a logical step after exploring funding options, the deal raises concerns about potential channel conflict for HPE, which recently spun off part of its consulting services. The acquisition brings HPE deeper into consulting, potentially competing with its existing channel and global alliance partners.

title: Disassembling Kodak
summary: This article analyzes Kodak's employment history, comparing its growth trajectory to modern tech giants like Apple, Amazon, and Google. It highlights how long it took Kodak to reach certain employment milestones versus the much faster growth experienced by today's leading tech companies, challenging the narrative that Kodak was a superior "innovation company" compared to Apple.

title: ServiceNow passes security test - now certified to hold AU Govt. info
summary: ServiceNow has achieved Australian Signals Directorate (ASD) certification for cloud services, allowing it to securely hold Australian Government Unclassified DLM information. This certification followed an independent audit of ServiceNow's staff, processes, technology, and Australian data centers, ensuring compliance with stringent government standards. The move is expected to boost confidence for local, state, and federal government agencies considering cloud adoption.

title: Obama Is Going on a Wall-Street Speaking Spree. Here's How Much Cash He's Raking In...
summary: Former President Barack Obama is earning significant speaking fees from financial institutions, with two confirmed events for $400,000 each. This practice is drawing some criticism, especially given his past rhetoric against Wall Street, and is similar to controversies faced by Hillary Clinton. Despite potential backlash, Obama's associates believe he isn't concerned as he is not running for office again.

title: HP Inc. Launches HP School Cloud to Improve Education Access in Developing World
summary: HP Inc. has launched the HP School Cloud as part of a $20 million learning investment, aiming to provide educational materials and apps to students, teachers, and adult learners in rural and underserved communities worldwide. This initiative leverages the HP Open Learning Platform and free, open-source educational materials to improve learning outcomes for 100 million people by 2025. HP is also partnering with Intel and Education Cannot Wait to distribute over 1,700 HP School Clouds and has launched other educational programs like AppFactory and HP Learning Studios in collaboration with Microsoft, UNHCR, and other organizations.

title: Arista Networks Makes its Hybrid Cloud Play, Extends EOS
summary: Arista Networks has introduced its Any Cloud software platform, extending its EOS to major public clouds like AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and Oracle Cloud, along with Microsoft Azure Stack. The platform integrates the new Arista vEOS Router and CloudVision functionality, including the new Cloud Tracer feature, to provide consistent architecture and operations across hybrid cloud environments. The platform is currently in beta and expected to be generally available on initial public clouds by the end of the year.

title: China is fast becoming a leading market for music
summary: Tencent's strategies have transformed China into a leading music market, with its streaming platforms boasting over 400 million users and an extensive music library. Headlining Music Matters 2017, CEO Cussion Pang highlighted how Tencent's initiatives have curtailed piracy, fostered subscriber growth, and leveraged social media integration for enhanced music experiences. While China's music revenue per capita is lower than the US and Japan, streaming is booming, and new genres like punk are gaining popularity.

title: Axioma names Nico Kicillof of Two Sigma and Microsoft as Managing Director
summary: Axioma has appointed Nico Kicillof, formerly of Two Sigma and Microsoft, to the newly created position of Managing Director, Head of Platform Engineering. His primary responsibility will be to streamline content flows into Axioma’s expanding suite of cloud-based products, leveraging his extensive engineering background to advance their cloud-based solutions. This strategic hire aims to enhance Axioma's offerings to financial institutions with robust, scalable, and modern data infrastructures.

title: HP uses artificial intelligence to transform its customer support experience
summary: HP Inc. has transformed its customer support experience by implementing a virtual agent built with the Microsoft Dynamics 365 AI solution for customer service. This AI solution helps customers solve common problems through conversational interaction and provides support staff with instant access to troubleshooting information, streamlining the support process for both customers and agents. The system also offers deeper insights into common customer issues, improving future products and services and driving increased customer loyalty.

title: Interbrand Releases 2017 Best Global Brands Report: Apple and Google Hold the Top Two Spots, while Ferrari, Netflix and Salesforce.com Enter the List
summary: Interbrand's 2017 Best Global Brands report names Apple and Google as the top two most valuable brands for the fifth consecutive year, with Microsoft coming in third. The report, themed "Growth in a Changing World," highlights technology as the dominant sector and includes new entrants Ferrari, Netflix, and Salesforce.com. The combined value of the Top 100 brands increased by 4.2% from 2016, reaching USD $1,871,730m.

title: How Mike Lazaridis wants to change your world with quantum computing
summary: Mike Lazaridis, former co-CEO of BlackBerry, is spearheading the development of a quantum technology hub in Waterloo, Ontario, aiming to lead the next technological revolution. Despite significant investments and the creation of research institutes, Canada's quantum sector faces an East-West rivalry with D-Wave Systems Inc. in British Columbia, which has already commercialized a quantum computer based on a different approach. The article explores the competing visions and challenges in establishing Canada as a leader in the nascent, multi-billion-dollar quantum computing industry.

title: Creating an innovation culture
summary: Waguih Ishak, Corning’s Silicon Valley technology chief, shares insights from his 40-year career on fostering an innovative culture. He emphasizes unconventional strategies like "innovation parenting," encouraging impractical ideas, and cultivating external relationships, rather than just focusing on obvious methods like investment or talent acquisition. The article also highlights the importance of managing project overload, hiring versatile individuals, and breaking hierarchical barriers to promote creativity and successful innovation.

title: Amazon says Google has pulled YouTube from Echo Show device
summary: Amazon announced that Google has inexplicably pulled YouTube from its Echo Show devices, causing a rare public dispute between the two tech giants. Google countered that Amazon's implementation of YouTube violated its terms of service, leading to a "broken user experience." This incident affects the Echo Show's video content and highlights ongoing competitive tensions in Silicon Valley.

title: Apple’s ‘Face ID’ Made in Taiwan｜Industry｜2017-10-02｜web only
summary: This article reveals that two Taiwanese companies, Himax and TSMC, are key suppliers for Apple's iPhone X Face ID technology. Himax provides tiny optical lenses for 3D facial recognition, while TSMC manufactures the near-infrared imaging sensor. The article also discusses Qualcomm's strategic efforts with Himax and TSMC to develop a competing 3D depth-sensing camera system for Android phones, indicating significant market opportunity for these Taiwanese firms.

title: Is Your Company Adapting Fast Enough to Thrive in an Increasingly Digital World?
summary: A new global survey by Harvard Business Review Analytic Services found that companies worldwide anticipate massive change due to digital technologies, yet many struggle to adapt quickly enough. Only a small percentage of organizations are considered "very digital," highlighting a significant challenge in transitioning to a rapidly evolving digital economy. The article outlines key steps, such as communicating strategy, building new structures, thinking in teams, experimenting, and rethinking IT, for companies to successfully capitalize on digital disruption.

title: Intel Offers Innovative Approach to IoT Scaling and Security
summary: Intel announced its Secure Device Onboard (Intel SDO) technology to address the challenges of scaling and securing IoT deployments. Intel SDO automates device onboarding, reducing setup time from hours to seconds and utilizing Intel Enhanced Privacy ID (Intel EPID) for anonymous authentication and secure communication. The technology is being adopted by other silicon providers and integrated into cloud platforms, with early successful implementation by Weatherford in the oil and gas sector.

title: PTC Announces a Major New Release to Vuforia Augmented Reality Platform
summary: PTC has announced Vuforia 7, a major new release to its Vuforia Augmented Reality Platform, introducing significant advancements like ground plane detection, next-generation object recognition with Model Targets, and broad support for Apple’s ARKit and Google’s ARCore via Vuforia Fusion. The update also launches Vuforia Chalk, an innovative app for collaborative visual communication directly on real-world objects. These enhancements aim to expand AR capabilities across more device types and environments, making AR development more accessible and powerful for developers.

title: Microsoft, GE sign agreement on new wind project in Ireland
summary: Microsoft announced a 15-year power purchase agreement with GE for a new 37-megawatt wind farm in County Kerry, Ireland. This project, which includes battery integration into wind turbines for energy storage, will help power Microsoft Cloud services and support the Irish grid. Microsoft is also acquiring an Irish energy supply license from GE, with ElectroRoute providing trading services.

title: Microsoft SharePoint recognized as a Leader in Gartner Magic Quadrant for Content Services Platforms
summary: Microsoft SharePoint has been recognized as a Leader in Gartner's 2017 Magic Quadrant for Content Services Platforms, specifically noted for its "Ability to Execute." The article highlights SharePoint's evolution from traditional ECM to dynamic content services, emphasizing its role as the foundational content platform for Office 365 and its ease of use, scalability, security, and broad file type support. This recognition underscores Microsoft's commitment to providing leading content services capabilities, driven by significant growth in SharePoint and OneDrive usage within Office 365.

title: Western Digital Aims Largest Hard Drive Ever at World’s Largest Data Centers
summary: Western Digital has developed the world's first 14TB hard drive, the HGST Ultrastar Hs14, specifically targeting hyper-scale cloud operators like Facebook, Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Tencent, and Alibaba. This new drive utilizes shingled magnetic recording (SMR) and fourth-generation HelioSeal technology to offer increased storage capacity and reduced power consumption, making it ideal for backup and archiving in large data centers. While Western Digital leads in introducing such high-capacity drives, competitors like Seagate Technology LLC and Toshiba Corp. are expected to follow suit.

title: How Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella disrupted the corporate retreat
summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella transformed the traditional corporate retreat by inviting new hires from recently acquired companies and scheduling customer visits to foster fresh perspectives. He recounts these changes in his book, "Hit Refresh," highlighting how these moves, initially met with resistance, ultimately led to more engaging and productive discussions focused on the company's future. Nadella's approach aimed to break through the conventional "talking at each other" dynamic of executive gatherings.

title: Augmented Reality Startup Magic Leap Raises $502M from Temasek & Co.
summary: Augmented reality startup Magic Leap Inc. has successfully raised $502 million in Series D equity funding, led by Singapore’s national wealth fund Temasek. This funding round included participation from new investors like EDBI and Grupo Globo, along with existing investors such as Alibaba Group and Google LLC, bringing their total raised capital to $1.4 billion. The company, which is developing a head-mounted virtual retinal display for 3D computer-generated imagery, is yet to release a product but may launch its first device priced between $1,500 and $2,000.

title: Barings Corporate Investors Declares Quarterly Dividend of $0.30 per Share
summary: Barings Corporate Investors announced a quarterly dividend of $0.30 per share, payable on November 10, 2017, to shareholders of record on October 30, 2017. The Trust also reported its Net Asset Value as of September 30, 2017, at $15.57 per share, and detailed its net investment income and realized capital gains for the recent quarter and year-to-date. Additionally, the company disclosed a refinancing agreement for its $30 million Senior Fixed Rate Convertible Note and a reduction in the minimum expected internal rate of return threshold for co-investment opportunities.

title: Intel, Samsung, Back Cybersecurity Startup Intezer
summary: Cybersecurity startup Intezer Labs Ltd. has raised $8 million in Series A funding led by Intel Capital, with participation from Magma Partners and existing investors Samsung NEXT and Alon Cohen. The company, founded in 2015, provides cybersecurity services by analyzing software for code similarities to detect and analyze malware, a technique successfully used in detecting WannaCry and NotPetya. Intezer plans to use this new funding to expand its global operations.

title: Meet Bill Boeing, the granddaddy of Seattle’s tech scene
summary: This article traces the surprising influence of William E. Boeing, founder of The Boeing Company, on Seattle's modern tech landscape. It highlights how Boeing, an entrepreneur from the early 20th century, shared characteristics with today's tech innovators like Jeff Bezos and Elon Musk, transforming Seattle into an economic powerhouse. The piece argues that Boeing's entrepreneurial spirit and vision laid the groundwork for the city's current tech success despite the company's eventual departure.

title: HPE to Stop Selling Commodity Servers to Hyper-Scale Cloud Companies
summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) is exiting the business of selling commodity servers to hyper-scale cloud providers like Amazon, Microsoft, and Alibaba. The company will instead focus on selling higher-margin hardware, such as high-end servers and hyper-converged infrastructure, to traditional enterprises and some tier-1 cloud players. This strategic shift is a response to the tough competition and low margins in the commodity server market, especially as cloud giants increasingly design their own hardware.

title: JAL Ventures Raises $60 Million for New Venture Capital Fund
summary: Israel-based JAL Ventures has announced a new $60 million venture capital fund. The fund will specifically target early-stage Israeli tech startups, with a primary focus on non-fatal defense technologies, SaaS, online services, communications, ecommerce, and security sectors. Notable investments will range from $3-5 million in companies with at least $1 million in annual sales, and the fund has already added three startups to its portfolio.

title: TCS, Palo Alto Networks team up to offer public cloud security services
summary: Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) and Palo Alto Networks have partnered to offer public cloud security services, enabling enterprises to securely migrate applications and data to the public cloud. These new services leverage Palo Alto Networks' Next-Generation Security Platform and TCS' global Security Operations Centres to protect against cyberthreats. The collaboration aims to provide comprehensive security, including consulting, audit, design, 24/7 operations, and threat analysis for public cloud environments.

title: Cisco and Google Find Mutual Interest in Cloud Computing (Published 2017)
summary: Google and Cisco Systems are partnering to help companies manage software and technology services across their own data centers and external cloud platforms. This collaboration allows Google to leverage Cisco's corporate ties to compete with Amazon in cloud services, while Cisco seeks to counter the threat cloud services pose to its traditional hardware business. Both companies, once dominant in different internet eras, are adapting to the evolving landscape of cloud computing.

title: Pat Stryker and President Trump Tie on List of Richest Billionaires
summary: Fort Collins resident Pat Stryker and President Donald Trump are tied for No. 248 on Forbes' list of America’s richest billionaires, each with an estimated net worth of $3.1 billion. They share this spot with 14 other individuals. The article also lists the top five wealthiest billionaires, with Bill Gates at number one.

title: Amazon, Google, Microsoft and Intel find billions more in profit
summary: Amazon, Google, Microsoft, and Intel significantly exceeded profit and revenue expectations in their third-quarter earnings reports. Collectively, these four tech giants increased their profits by approximately $2.2 billion and revenue by $19 billion compared to the previous year. Their stock prices rose in after-hours trading, further boosting their combined market capitalization.

title: Sonus, Microsoft Certified SBC provider, merges with Genband and renamed Ribbon Communications
summary: Sonus, a leading provider of certified gateways/session border controllers for Skype for Business, has completed its merger with Genband. The combined entity will be known as Ribbon Communications Inc., trading under the new ticker symbol RBBN by the end of 2017 while retaining the ticker SONS until then. This merger aims to create a significant global real-time communications organization, with Sonus customers expecting no immediate operational changes.

title: Microsoft announces one of the largest wind deals in the Netherlands with Vattenfall
summary: Microsoft has announced a significant wind energy deal with Vattenfall in the Netherlands, where it will purchase 100 percent of the wind energy generated from an expanded 180-megawatt wind farm adjacent to its local datacenter operations. This project, which will be constructed by Nuon (part of Vattenfall), aims to power Microsoft's cloud services with local, clean wind energy, contributing to Microsoft's global commitment to increase renewable energy use and creating economic opportunities. The agreement also leverages Microsoft Azure for Vattenfall's operations, strengthening the partnership in greening the cloud.

title: EA Sports UFC 3 Revealed With UFC® Lightweight Champion Conor McGregor as the Official Global Cover Athlete
summary: Electronic Arts (EA) officially announced EA SPORTS UFC 3, featuring UFC lightweight champion Conor McGregor as its global cover athlete. The game introduces "Real Player Motion (RPM) Tech" for fluid and responsive fighter motion and a new "G.O.A.T. Career Mode" where player choices outside the Octagon influence their path to becoming the Greatest of All Time. EA SPORTS UFC 3 is set for worldwide release on February 2, 2018, for Xbox One and PlayStation 4, with pre-order bonuses available for the Champions Edition.

title: Three years in a row – Microsoft is a leader in the ODBMS Magic Quadrant
summary: Microsoft has been positioned in the Leaders Quadrant of Gartner's 2017 Magic Quadrant for Operational Database Management Systems for the third consecutive year. This recognition highlights SQL Server's capabilities, including its cross-platform support (Windows, Linux, Docker containers), in-memory performance, mission-critical high availability, security features, and cost-competitiveness. The article encourages readers to review the full Gartner report and learn about free licenses for migrating to SQL Server 2017.

title: Ten trends redefining enterprise IT infrastructure
summary: The IT infrastructure landscape is experiencing rapid disruption, driven by ten key trends reshaping both provider and customer strategies. These trends include the shift to as-a-service models, mainstream adoption of public cloud, increased open-source usage, and evolving hardware and software architectures, presenting both opportunities and risks for industry players. The article highlights how familiar trends are accelerating and new developments are emerging, impacting cybersecurity, hardware sourcing, and the integration of AI and machine learning.

title: Commvault Executives Outline How 'Powerful Simplicity' Enables Enterprises to Use Data to Achieve Remarkable Things in Commvault GO 2017 Keynotes
summary: Commvault executives Bob Hammer and Al Bunte outlined how "powerful simplicity" and a shift from Information Technology to Data Technology enable enterprises to achieve remarkable things with data at Commvault GO 2017. Their keynotes highlighted the Commvault Data Platform and its innovations, such as Commvault HyperScale Technology, as solutions for accelerating digital transformation, reducing risk, and improving business outcomes amidst complex data environments. The conference featured customer success stories from organizations like Johns Hopkins University and Iowa Judicial, showcasing practical applications of Commvault's data management approach.

title: Microsoft Corporation is Deep in Artificial Intelligence Waters
summary: Microsoft Corporation is increasingly recognized as a major player in artificial intelligence, with its advanced AI chips making their way into devices like the HoloLens and plans for broader integration. The company is also leveraging its BrainWave platform for cloud-based AI acceleration and aims to make its AI technologies available to partners and Azure customers. The author contends that Microsoft's AI strategy is clearly defined and poised for significant revenue generation, making MSFT stock a strong investment in the AI industry.

title: Shift from Security to Civilian Market behind NICE Systems’ Growth
summary: NICE Systems, an Israeli company, has successfully transitioned from selling surveillance software to governments to providing call center systems for enterprises. This strategic shift, spearheaded by CEO Barak Eilam, has led to increased revenue and profit margins, driven by key acquisitions like inContact. The company’s recent Q3 results indicate the new strategy is paying off.

title: Kroger is using Google and Microsoft clouds to avoid paying Amazon
summary: Kroger, the largest grocery store chain, is strategically splitting its cloud computing investments between Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud, deliberately avoiding Amazon Web Services (AWS) due to competitive concerns following Amazon's acquisition of Whole Foods. Chris Hjelm, Kroger's CIO, stated that it doesn't make competitive sense to help grow Amazon's business. This move mirrors actions by other large retailers like Walmart and Target, who are also seeking alternative cloud providers.

title: Microsoft buys Chevron's data center in San Antonio to fuel its cloud
summary: Microsoft Corp. has acquired Chevron Corp.'s data center in San Antonio, a deal that closed last month. This acquisition is part of Chevron's strategy to move away from operating its own corporate data center and instead leverage Microsoft's cloud services. The move highlights Microsoft's expansion in the cloud computing market, with other related articles discussing Microsoft's Azure Stack and Rackspace's support for Microsoft's cloud initiatives.

title: Kroger avoids the Amazon machine, prefers Google and Microsoft clouds
summary: Kroger announced the expansion of its cloud computing portfolio on the Google Cloud Platform, adding to existing contracts with Microsoft Azure and Pivotal. The grocery giant is actively avoiding AWS due to competitive reasons, especially after Amazon's acquisition of Whole Foods. Kroger is also forming a "cloud enablement team" to manage these new cloud operations.

title: IBM raises pressure on rivals with quantum computer prototype
summary: IBM has announced the creation of a prototype 50-qubit quantum computer, raising the stakes in the race with Google to commercialize quantum computing technology. This development is nearing the "quantum supremacy" threshold, where quantum computers could perform tasks beyond the reach of conventional supercomputers. The article highlights the ongoing challenges, such as reducing error rates, but also the rapid advancement of the technology with several companies, including Microsoft and D-Wave Systems, also active in the field.

title: First bank in Singapore to launch new cloud-based data centre test
summary: DBS Bank announced a partnership with Equinix to transform one of its Singapore data centers into a cloud-optimized center test, significantly reducing its size and operating costs by 75%. This initiative supports DBS's commitment to sustainability by improving energy efficiency and aligns with its strategy to adopt cloud technologies for enhanced agility, scalability, and digital transformation. DBS has been actively migrating to cloud-optimized technology, resulting in substantial efficiency gains and increased capacity, and aims to shift 50% of its compute workload to the public cloud by 2018.

title: Business Alumni, Partners to be Honored at 2018 Hall of Fame Gala

summary: Amazon's cloud computing unit is expanding its operations in China through a new partnership with Ningxia Western Cloud Data Technology Co Ltd (NWCD). title: Microsoft Unified Support Bringing Increased Costs for Organizations
summary: Microsoft's Unified Support plan is replacing other support plans, including Premier Support, and is expected to lead to substantial price increases for organizations. Gartner Inc. estimates these increased costs and notes that Unified Support ties costs to an organization's overall consumption of Microsoft online services and Software Assurance payments. While Microsoft claims most customers will see little to no increases and gain new services, experts suggest it may introduce a "new Microsoft tax" for many organizations.

Microsoft and Oracle remain leaders, but Amazon Web Services has gained ground, while several previous providers were axed. The report highlights machine learning, serverless scenarios, and streaming integration as defining features of current tools and anticipates machine learning capabilities will drive future innovation in this mature market.

title: IBM experiments with quantum computing; signs Samsung, JPMorgan in tie-ups
summary: IBM has partnered with Samsung, JPMorgan Chase & Co., and other companies to experiment with quantum computing and expand its applications. IBM is also giving early access to its quantum computers to help companies become familiar with the technology for future, more powerful machines.

title: John Chambers leaves behind a legacy of growth and disappointment at Cisco
summary: John Chambers, former CEO and chairman of Cisco Systems, retired leaving a mixed legacy of immense growth during the internet boom and later struggles as the company adapted to new technologies. These investments align with Abry's strategy to address the increasing technology demands of the SMB market, particularly concerning cloud adoption, cybersecurity, and competitiveness.

title: HoloTouch Claims Microsoft Willfully Infringing Holographic, Human-Machine Interface Patents
summary: HoloTouch, Inc. has filed a lawsuit against Microsoft Corporation, alleging willful patent infringement related to holographic and human-machine interface technologies. HoloTouch asserts that Microsoft's HoloLens product infringes on two of its patents, U.S. Patent No. 6377238 and U.S. Patent No. 7054045, despite Microsoft's prior knowledge of these patents and refusal to engage in licensing discussions. HoloTouch's technology, developed in the mid-1990s, addresses issues in HMI by enabling touchless control and reducing power consumption and size.
